raw: Act 1, Scene 3 — Room in Capulet’s House

sentences.en: Room in Capulet’s House

summary.en: Lady Capulet and the Nurse tell Juliet that Paris wants to marry her. Juliet agrees to look at him at the party.
summary.ko: 캐퓰릿 부인과 유모가 줄리엣에게 패리스가 청혼했다고 알린다. 줄리엣은 잔치에서 그를 한번 보겠다고 한다.

raw: Enter Lady Capulet and Nurse.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Nurse, where’s my daughter? Call her forth to me.

sentences.en: Nurse, where is my daughter?
Call her to me.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Now, by my maidenhead, at twelve year old,
I bade her come. What, lamb! What ladybird!
God forbid! Where’s this girl? What, Juliet!

sentences.en: I swear by the virginity I had at twelve years old, I told her to come.
sentences.ko: 열두 살 때 제 순결을 걸고 말씀드리는데, 오라고 했어요.

sentences.en: Come, my lamb! Come, my ladybird!
sentences.ko: 이리 오렴, 우리 어린 양! 우리 무당벌레 아가씨!

sentences.en: God forbid! Where is this girl? Juliet!

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw: How now, who calls?

sentences.en: Who is calling me?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Your mother.

sentences.en: Your mother.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Madam, I am here. What is your will?

sentences.en: Madam, I am here.
What would you like?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
This is the matter. Nurse, give leave awhile,
We must talk in secret. Nurse, come back again,
I have remember’d me, thou’s hear our counsel.
Thou knowest my daughter’s of a pretty age.

sentences.en: This is the matter.
Nurse, leave us for a moment because we must talk in secret.
sentences.ko: 유모, 비밀로 이야기해야 하니 잠시 자리를 비켜줘.

sentences.en: Nurse, come back again.
I have changed my mind and you should hear our private talk.
sentences.ko: 생각해 보니 유모도 우리 이야기를 들어야겠어.

sentences.en: You know my daughter is getting quite grown up.
sentences.ko: 유모도 알다시피 내 딸이 이제 꽤 컸잖아.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Faith, I can tell her age unto an hour.

sentences.en: I can tell her age to the hour.
sentences.ko: 정확히 몇 살인지 말씀드릴 수 있어요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: She’s not fourteen.

sentences.en: She is not fourteen.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I’ll lay fourteen of my teeth,
And yet, to my teen be it spoken, I have but four,
She is not fourteen. How long is it now
To Lammas-tide?

sentences.en: I would bet fourteen of my teeth that she is not fourteen.
sentences.ko: 제 이빨 열네 개를 걸고 말하는데, 그 애는 아직 열네 살이 안 됐어요.

sentences.en: Sadly, I have only four teeth.
How long is it until the harvest festival?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: A fortnight and odd days.

sentences.en: It is about two weeks and a few days.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Even or odd, of all days in the year,
Come Lammas Eve at night shall she be fourteen.
Susan and she,—God rest all Christian souls!—
Were of an age. Well, Susan is with God;
She was too good for me. But as I said,
On Lammas Eve at night shall she be fourteen;
That shall she, marry; I remember it well.
’Tis since the earthquake now eleven years;
And she was wean’d,—I never shall forget it—,
Of all the days of the year, upon that day:
For I had then laid wormwood to my dug,
Sitting in the sun under the dovehouse wall;
My lord and you were then at Mantua:
Nay, I do bear a brain. But as I said,
When it did taste the wormwood on the nipple
Of my dug and felt it bitter, pretty fool,
To see it tetchy, and fall out with the dug!
Shake, quoth the dovehouse: ’twas no need, I trow,
To bid me trudge.
And since that time it is eleven years;
For then she could stand alone; nay, by th’rood
She could have run and waddled all about;
For even the day before she broke her brow,
And then my husband,—God be with his soul!
A was a merry man,—took up the child:
‘Yea,’ quoth he, ‘dost thou fall upon thy face?
Thou wilt fall backward when thou hast more wit;
Wilt thou not, Jule?’ and, by my holidame,
The pretty wretch left crying, and said ‘Ay’.
To see now how a jest shall come about.
I warrant, and I should live a thousand years,
I never should forget it. ‘Wilt thou not, Jule?’ quoth he;
And, pretty fool, it stinted, and said ‘Ay.’

sentences.en: Even day or odd day, she will be fourteen.
sentences.ko: 홀수일이든 짝수일이든, 그날이면 정확히 열네 살이 돼요.

sentences.en: It will be on the night before the harvest festival.
sentences.ko: 추수 축제 전날 밤이 될 거예요.

sentences.en: Susan and she were the same age.
God rest all Christian souls!
Susan is with God now.
She was too good for me.
But as I said, she will be fourteen on that night.
sentences.ko: 하지만 말씀드린 대로, 그날 밤이면 열네 살이 돼요.

sentences.en: Yes, I remember it well.
It has been eleven years since the earthquake.
That was the day she stopped breastfeeding.
I will never forget it.
I had put a bitter plant on my breast to stop her nursing.
sentences.ko: 아이가 젖을 떼게 하려고 제 가슴에 쓴 약초를 올려두었거든요.

sentences.en: I sat in the sun under the wall of the pigeon house.
sentences.ko: 비둘기 집 담벼락 아래 햇볕을 받으며 앉아 있었어요.

sentences.en: You and your husband were in Mantua, a nearby city, then.
sentences.ko: 그때 마님과 주인님은 근처 도시인 만토바에 계셨죠.

sentences.en: No, I have a good memory.
But as I said, she tasted the bitter plant on my breast.
sentences.ko: 하지만 말씀드렸듯이, 아이는 제 가슴에서 쓴 약초 맛을 보았어요.

sentences.en: The sweet little fool found it bitter.
sentences.ko: 그 귀여운 바보가 그게 쓰다고 느낀 거죠.

sentences.en: She got cross and pushed my breast away!
sentences.ko: 아이는 화를 내며 제 가슴을 밀쳐냈어요!

sentences.en: Then the pigeon house shook from the earthquake.
Nobody needed to tell me to run!
sentences.ko: 누가 말해주지 않아도 도망쳐야 한다는 걸 알았어요!

sentences.en: And since that time, eleven years have passed.
She could stand alone then.
sentences.ko: 그때 아이는 혼자 설 수 있었어요.

sentences.en: No, by the cross, she could run and walk around.
sentences.ko: 아니요, 십자가를 걸고 맹세코, 아이는 뛰고 걸어 다닐 수 있었어요.

sentences.en: Just the day before, she fell and cut her forehead.
Then my husband, God be with his soul!
sentences.ko: 그때 제 남편이, 하늘에서 편히 쉬기를!

sentences.en: He was a happy man.
He picked up the child.
He asked, 'Yes, did you fall on your face?'
He said, 'You will fall backward when you are older.'
sentences.ko: 그분은 '네가 더 크면 뒤로 넘어지게 될 거야'라고 말씀하셨어요.

sentences.en: He asked, 'Will you not, Jule?'
The poor little thing stopped crying and said, 'Yes.'
Look how that joke turned out.
I promise I would never forget it even if I lived a thousand years.
sentences.ko: 천 년을 산다 해도 절대 잊지 못할 거예요.

sentences.en: He asked, 'Will you not, Jule?'
sentences.ko: 그 사람이 '안 그럴 거니, 줄리?'라고 물었죠.

sentences.en: And the sweet little fool stopped crying and said, 'Yes.'
sentences.ko: 그리고 그 귀여운 어린아이는 울음을 그치고 '네'라고 대답했어요.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Enough of this; I pray thee hold thy peace.

sentences.en: That is enough.
Please be quiet.

speaker: NURSE

sentences.en: Yes, madam.
But I cannot help laughing.
I laugh to think she stopped crying and said 'Yes'.
sentences.ko: 아이가 울음을 그치고 '네'라고 대답한 게 생각나서 웃음이 나요.

sentences.en: She had a bump on her head as big as a young rooster's testicle.
sentences.ko: 머리에 어린 수탉의 고환만큼이나 큰 혹이 났었거든요.

sentences.en: It was a hard hit, and she cried bitterly.
sentences.ko: 세게 부딪힌 거라 아이가 아주 서럽게 울었죠.

sentences.en: My husband asked, 'Yes, did you fall on your face?'
He said, 'You will fall backward when you are older.'
sentences.ko: 그는 '네가 더 크면 뒤로 넘어지게 될 거야'라고 말했고요.

sentences.en: He asked, 'Will you not, Jule?'
She stopped crying and said, 'Yes.'

speaker: JULIET
raw: And stint thou too, I pray thee, Nurse, say I.

sentences.en: Please be quiet now too, Nurse.
That is what I say.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Peace, I have done. God mark thee to his grace
Thou wast the prettiest babe that e’er I nurs’d:
And I might live to see thee married once, I have my wish.

sentences.en: Peace, I am finished.
May God bless you.
You were the prettiest baby that I ever nursed.
sentences.ko: 너는 내가 돌본 아이들 중 가장 예쁜 아기였단다.

sentences.en: I hope to live long enough to see you married once.
sentences.ko: 네가 결혼하는 걸 한 번이라도 볼 수 있을 만큼 오래 살고 싶구나.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Marry, that marry is the very theme
I came to talk of. Tell me, daughter Juliet,
How stands your disposition to be married?

sentences.en: Well, marriage is exactly what I came to talk about.
sentences.ko: 그래, 바로 그 결혼 얘기를 하러 왔단다.

sentences.en: Tell me, daughter Juliet, how do you feel about getting married?
sentences.ko: 말해 보렴, 줄리엣, 결혼에 대해 어떻게 생각하니?

speaker: JULIET
raw: It is an honour that I dream not of.

sentences.en: It is an honor that I do not dream of.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
An honour! Were not I thine only nurse,
I would say thou hadst suck’d wisdom from thy teat.

sentences.en: An honor!
If I were not your only nurse, I would say you drank wisdom from my breast.
sentences.ko: 내가 네 유모가 아니었다면, 네가 내 젖을 통해 지혜를 마셨다고 말했을 거야.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Well, think of marriage now: younger than you,
Here in Verona, ladies of esteem,
Are made already mothers. By my count
I was your mother much upon these years
That you are now a maid. Thus, then, in brief;
The valiant Paris seeks you for his love.

sentences.en: Well, think about marriage now.
sentences.ko: 자, 이제 결혼에 대해 생각해 보렴.

sentences.en: In Verona, many respected ladies younger than you are already mothers.
sentences.ko: 베로나에서는 너보다 어린 많은 귀부인들이 이미 어머니가 되었단다.

sentences.en: I was your mother at about the same age that you are now as a girl.
sentences.ko: 나도 네 나이 때 어머니가 되었어.

sentences.en: So, in short, the brave Paris seeks you for his love.
sentences.ko: 그러니까 한마디로, 용감한 패리스가 너에게 청혼했어.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
A man, young lady! Lady, such a man
As all the world—why he’s a man of wax.

sentences.en: A man, young lady!
Lady, such a man that the whole world—
Why, he is as perfect as a wax statue.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Verona’s summer hath not such a flower.

sentences.en: Verona's summer does not have such a flower.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Nay, he’s a flower, in faith a very flower.

sentences.en: No, he is a flower. Truly, he is a very beautiful flower.
sentences.ko: 아니요, 그는 꽃이에요. 정말로 아주 아름다운 꽃이죠.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
What say you, can you love the gentleman?
This night you shall behold him at our feast;
Read o’er the volume of young Paris’ face,
And find delight writ there with beauty’s pen.
Examine every married lineament,
And see how one another lends content;
And what obscur’d in this fair volume lies,
Find written in the margent of his eyes.
This precious book of love, this unbound lover,
To beautify him, only lacks a cover:
The fish lives in the sea; and ’tis much pride
For fair without the fair within to hide.
That book in many’s eyes doth share the glory,
That in gold clasps locks in the golden story;
So shall you share all that he doth possess,
By having him, making yourself no less.

sentences.en: What do you say? Can you love the gentleman?
sentences.ko: 어떻게 생각하니? 이 신사를 사랑할 수 있겠니?

sentences.en: You will see him at our feast tonight.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 우리 잔치에서 그를 보게 될 거야.

sentences.en: Read the book of young Paris's face.
Find beauty written there.
Look at every feature of his face.
sentences.ko: 그의 얼굴에 있는 모든 특징을 살펴보렴.

sentences.en: See how each part fits together perfectly.
sentences.ko: 각 부분이 얼마나 완벽하게 어우러지는지 봐라.

sentences.en: Look for what is hidden in this beautiful book.
sentences.ko: 이 아름다운 책 속에 숨겨진 것을 찾아봐.

sentences.en: Find it written in the edges of his eyes.
sentences.ko: 그것은 그의 눈가에 쓰여 있을 거야.

sentences.en: This precious book of love, this unbound lover, only needs a cover to be beautiful.
sentences.ko: 이 소중한 사랑의 책, 아직 묶이지 않은 이 연인에게는 표지만 있으면 돼.

sentences.en: A fish lives in the sea.
It is a fine thing when a beautiful cover holds a beautiful story inside.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 표지가 아름다운 이야기를 담고 있으면 정말 멋진 일이지.

sentences.en: Many people see the glory of a story locked in gold clasps.
sentences.ko: 많은 사람들은 금 걸쇠로 잠긴 황금빛 이야기를 칭송한단다.

sentences.en: You will share everything that he has.
sentences.ko: 너는 그가 가진 모든 것을 공유하게 될 거야.

sentences.en: By having him, you will not become less important.
sentences.ko: 그와 함께함으로써 네 가치가 낮아지는 일은 없을 거야.

speaker: NURSE
raw: No less, nay bigger. Women grow by men.

sentences.en: Not less, no, much more.
Women grow by being with men.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Speak briefly, can you like of Paris’ love?

sentences.en: Speak briefly.
Can you accept Paris's love?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I’ll look to like, if looking liking move:
But no more deep will I endart mine eye
Than your consent gives strength to make it fly.

sentences.en: I will try to like him if looking at him makes me like him.
sentences.ko: 그를 보고 호감이 생긴다면 좋아해 볼게요.

sentences.en: But I will not look deeper than your permission allows.
sentences.ko: 하지만 허락하신 범위 이상으로는 깊이 보지 않을게요.

sentences.en: I will only go as far as your consent lets me.

raw: Enter a Servant.

speaker: SERVANT
raw:
Madam, the guests are come, supper served up, you called, my young lady
asked for, the Nurse cursed in the pantry, and everything in extremity.
I must hence to wait, I beseech you follow straight.

sentences.en: Madam, the guests have arrived and supper is served.
sentences.ko: 마님, 손님들이 도착하셨고 저녁 식사가 준비되었습니다.

sentences.en: You called for me.
Everyone is asking for my young lady.
The Nurse was scolded in the pantry.
Everything is in a crazy rush.
I must leave now, so please follow me immediately.
sentences.ko: 지금 바로 가야 하니 즉시 저를 따라오십시오.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: We follow thee.

sentences.en: We are following you.

raw: Exit Servant.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw: Juliet, the County stays.

sentences.en: Juliet, Count Paris is waiting.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Go, girl, seek happy nights to happy days.

sentences.en: Go, girl.
Go and find happy nights to go with your happy days.
sentences.ko: 가서 행복한 낮에 어울리는 행복한 밤을 찾으렴.

raw: Exeunt.
